selections.comment: Denied by just a nose in a novices' hurdle at Newcastle last month, DOUBLE DIGITS is the obvious starting point and a repeat of that performance would make the son of Mastercraftsman the one to beat. Kabuki has something to find on a literal reading of the official ratings and was well held on his return from wind surgery at Sedgefield 28 days ago. Therefore, recent point-to-point winner, Kimjoy, rates a bigger danger to the selection now he is back under Rules.

selections.comment: New Invention ran promisingly when introduced in a Newcastle maiden in February and is one to keep an eye on in the betting. Similar comments apply to point-to-point winner Theatre Light, who makes her Rules debut at a realistic level and could have a big say if she adapts to hurdles. Nevertheless, this is probably best left to CAHIER'S DEN, who has filled the runner-up spot in deeper races on his last two starts and has a big chance of going one better this time.

selections.comment: SEAN OG, who is already a three-time winner over fences, is resilient and this should provide the Dianne Sayer-trained gelding with a sufficient stamina test to draw the best out of him. With Mt Fugi Park (first-time cheekpieces) and Moon Over Mexico (first start after wind surgery) both having something to prove, Finn Lough is the most obvious danger to the selection, despite running off 4lb higher than for his recent handicap win at Southwell.

selections.comment: IMPERIAL JADE arrives at the top of her game. An impressive winner at Doncaster in February, Charlie Longsdon's inmate defied an 8lb hike to follow up at Huntingdon and the hat-trick beckons with the underfoot conditions remaining in her favour. Willaston has eased to an attractive mark and drops in class with a shout, while The Navigator was winning off today's mark last autumn and could bounce back on the forecast good ground.

selections.comment: Revitalised after a short break, POWEROFJET recorded his first success with a convincing win here last month. He looked to have plenty left in the tank and a 5lb rise may not be enough to anchor the improving six-year-old. Looking Splendid looked likely to finish in the places when falling at the last at Newcastle and can have a say in the outcome, while Breadalbane Lass ran well for second here in February and could feature again with a similar effort.

selections.comment: SUPER CITIZEN has put together a string of solid enough performances to suggest this drop in class could provide him with a deserved return to winning ways. Martalmix'jac gets 13lb from the selection and is an obvious threat with Tabiath Worsley claiming an additional 3lb from the saddle. Gipsy Lee Rose and Whosmydaddy have course experience to draw upon and it would come as no surprise to see at least the former stage a revival back here.

selections.comment: PASSENGERONTHESHIP and Wee Alki have both hinted that their turns are close to hand and appear to be the pair to focus on. At this stage, the former, with his stamina more proven from his point-to-point days, is the more experienced of the pair and could find the requisite improvement now he tackles this sort of trip for the first time under Rules. The latter is still of low-milage and could also develop as a stayer in time. Rob Roy Macgregor and On We Go complete the shortlist.

selections.comment: STRONG WARRIOR made a winning debut over the minimum trip at Ayr last summer. The son of Mehmas beat only three rivals but all three have subsequently won, so Richard Fahey's charge looks to have strong claims of defying a penalty on the strength of that form. Veblen Good is a more recent winner, having scored at Wolverhampton in October, and he could prove a threat, while U Sure Do and newcomer Call Me Betty are others to note.

selections.comment: DETROIT LION posted his best effort to date when upped to 1m3f at Southwell and finishing a respectable second. This extra distance may bring further progress and Joe Leavy's 3lb allowance relieves some of the burden of carrying top weight. Ribble River ended last season with a double and there should be more to come from him this year, while Letmeseethecolts returned to turf with a good effort at Doncaster last month and could have a say in proceedings.

selections.comment: It was heavy underfoot when Justus won last year's renewal of this contest and he's not easily dismissed on this faster surface, but PIGEON HOUSE makes most appeal. The son of Saxon Warrior returned to the Flat with a fine second in an amateur riders' race at Musselburgh only six days ago and is taken to go one better competing off the same mark. C&D winner Glory And Honour makes most appeal of the remainder.

selections.comment: Tim Easterby plays a potentially strong hand with Vince L'Amour and Manila Scouse capable players based on their peak form. However, it has been a relatively quiet spell for the yard and the betting market should be helpful here. Even so, this could go to the less exposed VENTURE CAPITAL, whose three-year-old season was full of promise. Kevin Ryan's progressive gelding could be hard to beat if picking up where left off in October. Previous C&D winners Ventura Express and Dream Composer are others solid contenders.

selections.comment: CAYMAN TAI showed promise as a juvenile and progressed nicely as 2024 unfolded. Last seen when a respectable seventh in a valuable nursery at York in August, this could be an ideal piece of placement by Richard Hannon for the returning son of Earthlight, who takes a drop back down in class today. Fan Mail and Lesley's Boy run for yards with very healthy strike-rates at this venue, with the latter being especially notable given Richard Fahey won four consecutive renewals of this race from 2015 to 2019.

selections.comment: DODDIE'S IMPACT is match-fit from a light all-weather campaigns and the still low-mileage four-year-old gets the vote back on turf from just 1lb above his only previous winning mark. Mrs Trump handled this course well on her most recent start and, having won when fresh last May, another bold showing looks likely. South Shore is also noted from a workable mark, while similar applies to One More Dream despite his turf record of 1-16 being a worry.

selections.comment: Partisan Hero won over a mile at Kempton in February and looks set for a bold double bid, but a 3lb higher mark may just catch him out now back on turf and preference is for SHALADAR. A neck second off 2lb higher over 1m at Ascot in September, Kevin Ryan's gelding has slipped to a handy mark and he could capitalise if ready to roll on his seasonal debut. Finn Russell completes the shortlist.

selections.comment: LEDNIKOV saves his best for this track and looks worth sticking with. He was winning for the fourth time here when successful on his latest start, having also beaten Moon Over The Sea here in February. The latter boosted that form by winning at Wolverhampton last week, while Ana Emaraaty had the measure of Rubellite (third) when scoring over 1m2f at Newcastle a fortnight ago and Jim Goldie's charge is another to consider.

selections.comment: Ballarat Bertie opened his account with last month's victory at Wolverhampton, though it's far from certain this drop back in distance will suit. Perfect Parole is marginally preferred to the latter, given she won over the extended mile at Wolverhampton in February, but the steadily improving I CAN BOOGY may prove the one to side with. Nigel Tinkler's filly snatched second in the dying strides over 7f at Newcastle last time and that encouraging effort suggests she will see out this longer trip.

selections.comment: ALONDRA finished fifth over 6f at Newmarket on last year's debut, but failed build on that promising effort during the rest of the season. However, she returned to action with a creditable fourth at Wolverhampton on her first start over the minimum trip, and the daughter of Sergei Prokofiev may prove a more attractive proposition this term. Radio Star went close at Nottingham when last seen at the track and she can get involved, while Queensmaite is a newcomer worthy of a second glance.

selections.comment: Party Bear successfully stepped up to 7f at Southwell last month and has been given a chance to follow up off 4lb higher. Zizi and Calaxy also arrive on the back of winning efforts and merit betting checks on their seasonal/handicap debuts. However, it would dangerous to underestimate ART PATRON, a full-sister to the classy Eternally who could be well placed to emulate her sibling by making a winning start to her three-year-old campaign.

selections.comment: NAZUKI was the ready winner of a similar race over this C&D in November and, having been given time to strengthen up since, the daughter of Earthlight is an attractive proposition as she bids to follow up. Vamp and American Treasure both have a more recent run under their belt and they look the main opposition, with the former rated the chief danger given the latter, as the only four-year-old, is disadvantaged at weights on these terms.

selections.comment: BILLY MCGARRY had been knocking on the door prior to his recent C&D success and the six-year-old boasts strong credentials once again, especially with his rider's 7lb allowance to aid his cause. Mickey Mongoose's latest efforts have been consistent and another solid effort appears to be on the cards. Others to consider include Disclosure, who carries a 5lb penalty after winning at Lingfield last Tuesday, and Jack Daniel.

selections.comment: A contest that might prove to be informative in the coming months with plenty of unexposed types. PHILANTHROPIST improved with each start as a juvenile and James Fanshawe's gelding scored at the third attempt on the all-weather at Newcastle. Now sent handicapping, it wouldn't be a surprise to see further improvement. Prince Of India has the benefit of a run under his belt after a novice victory at Wolverhampton and commands plenty of respect, while Kirkdale, Platinum Crystal and Stenmark appeal most of the remainder.
